hook: Internal email chain between AFOSI intelligence oversight staff and an OUSD(I&S) Information Disclosure Analyst, negotiating how to downgrade an IIR from SECRET//NOFORN to UNCLASSIFIED so it can be used in a product — with the UNCLASS summary of the underlying sighting embedded in the chain.
why_it_matters: The document reveals the bureaucratic mechanics of UAP disclosure: rather than full declassification (which requires AFOSI Commander signature), officials found a faster path via 'derivative classification review,' suggesting institutional workarounds are being developed to release UAP material. The embedded IIR summary describes a large blue triangular object observed for eight minutes near a national security facility, recorded on a civilian's phone — the kind of near-facility sighting that triggers the most sensitive reporting channels. The fact that the original report was classified SECRET//NOFORN before this review underscores that even civilian UAP encounters near sensitive sites are treated as classified intelligence.
key_findings: A civilian observer reported a large, blue, featureless triangular object hovering near a national security facility in the Pacific Time Zone at night in March 2023 for approximately eight minutes, captured on a personal cellular device.

The object's movement was described as 'backing up' in a 'jerking' or 'jumping' manner the reporter explicitly contrasted with 'smooth' jet propulsion — the reporter also stated they did not believe it was a drone.

The reporter specifically noted the absence of several expected features: no defined flight path, no vapor trail, no apparent cloaking capabilities, and no visible photo or data collection equipment — these negatives are preserved in the UNCLASS summary.

The underlying Intelligence Information Report (IIR) was originally classified SECRET//NOFORN; release required navigating AFOSI's formal process, which the OSI CI Collections and Operations PM acknowledged was a novel situation for them.

Approval was granted by the OSI CI Collections and Operations PM / Intelligence Oversight PM to use the UNCLASS summary in an unspecified product, with the IIR and a draft report noted as attachments to the originating email.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The disclosure pipeline — IIR processed through OUSD(I&S) for use in an unspecified 'product' — reflects the post-2022 AARO-era infrastructure for declassifying and publishing UAP reports.

AFOSI (Air Force Office of Special Investigations), whose CI Collections and Operations PM is the approving authority here, has historically operated out of Wright-Patterson and remains the Air Force's primary UAP collection and counterintelligence arm.
The effort to convert a SECRET//NOFORN IIR into an UNCLASSIFIED summary suitable for external use aligns with congressional mandates for UAP transparency passed in the FY2023–2024 NDAAs.
